CLAUDE.md — datarium

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

datarium is the founder’s teaching-dataset package (the D-51 “book’s taught dataset” spine for the Datanovia lessons). It ships curated data frames — no function code.

This file is the always-on policy loaded every session. Invoked procedures live in .claude/skills/ (issue-fixing, cran-submission, revdep-check); they reference the policy here.

Plan of record: pkgs/_roadmaps/datarium_feature_roadmap.md (prioritized, adversarially-reviewed). Read it before any change. Its keystone: cut a CRAN release (0.2.0) — several taught datasets are GitHub-only, so the install.packages("datarium") teaching flywheel is broken until then.

Non-regression policy (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

For a data-only package, “non-regression” means byte-identity of the shipped .rda files and stability of every dataset’s structure — lessons and committed Quarto freezes depend on the exact bytes.

  1. NEVER change an existing dataset’s values or structure — no change to values, column names, types, factor levels/order, or row order. Doc improvements are text-only (roxygen .R → .Rd). New datasets are purely additive.
  2. NEVER recompress the data. Do not run tools::resaveRdaFiles or R CMD build --resave-data (both change bytes). Write a data/*.rda only when deliberately adding a NEW dataset, via its data-raw/ / inst/data.R generator + usethis::use_data(<name>).
  3. Prove no regression. There is no test suite and no function code, so the gate is R CMD check (the R-CMD-check Action). After any change, confirm git status shows no data/*.rda modified and the check is clean (0/0/0).
  4. Dependency-free / webR-light forever — lessons load datarium live in-browser; never add a non-base dependency. Depends is base R only; NAMESPACE is an empty roxygen stub; LazyData: true.
  5. A change that must alter an existing dataset is not a “fix” — flag it explicitly and get maintainer sign-off; never let it pass quietly.

Every dataset ships the full doc bundle

@format \describe{} (each variable + units + factor levels) · @source (real vs simulated — honestly) · @references · a base-R @examples running the canonical analysis. Several current stubs are minimal (name/format/examples only); bringing them up to the full bundle is text-only doc work (a roadmap keystone) and must not touch .rda bytes.

Evaluate before implementing

Not every request warrants a change. Prefer a text-only doc fix or an existing dataset over new data; a new dataset must earn its place in a lesson. Record a one-line justification, or decline with a reasoned reply.

Every documented claim must be verifiable (NON-NEGOTIABLE — credibility is the asset)

A dataset’s doc is a factual assertion a user relies on in teaching and papers. - Verify docs against the actual object: data(<name>); str(<name>) — the @format dims, every variable, and every factor level must match what ships. Row/column counts in @format are claims; check them. - @source must be truthful: never label simulated data as real or real data as simulated. Simulated sets are built with set.seed() in their generator (reproducible) — say so. - Never ship an unchecked universal quantifier (“every/all/only”) in a doc without enumerating the set.

Output verification before posting (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

datarium ships data, so a reply/reprex shows the dataset and (usually) its canonical base-R analysis. Before posting anything (issue, PR, comment, or to the user): reason from the data to a prediction, then confirm it. - Run data("<name>") and confirm the printed structure/values match the claim (dims, factor levels, a value). - Run every analysis snippet end-to-end — don’t paste illustrative code unrun. - If the reply includes a plot, open and view the rendered image; every caption must be true of the pixels. “It loads / it ran” is not enough.

Issue-fixing discipline (anti-drift)

Full process in the issue-fixing skill; the essentials that keep us from drifting: - Read the issue’s IMAGES and its ENTIRE comment thread (gh issue view <N> --repo kassambara/datarium --comments), not just the OP — address every sub-ask. - Verify against the CURRENT data by exercising it (data()/str()/the canonical analysis), not a proxy. - Two independent adversarial reviewers before ANY close — fresh read-only subagents, run separately, each tasked to refute “fully resolved and safe to close.” Both must clear it. - No close and no dataset change without the maintainer’s explicit approval on anything behavior-changing.

Writing style — no AI fluff (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

Everything written for a human — issue replies, PR/commit text, NEWS, messages to the user — must read as if the maintainer wrote it. - No boilerplate / form-letters, no marketing / self-congratulation, no AI tells (no emoji, no “Great question!”, no “It’s worth noting that…”, no bolded buzzword lists). - No second-person / assistant voice in durable artifacts — write “Decisions to take”, never “Decisions for you” / “Here’s what I did” / “Let me know if…”. - No meta-argument against a road not taken inside a PR body — the PR states the decision; the debate belongs in the issue thread or the roadmap. - Don’t surface internal QA machinery in public text (“adversarial review”, “byte-identity gate”, coverage %). - A commit/PR body contains: what changed, why, the user-facing effect, Fixes #N / Refs #N. Nothing else.

Prior-art, credit & naming another package

Naming a package is fine when factual — a dependency you build on, or a neutral validation cross-check (“results match DescTools::X”). The risk is reproducing a rival’s distinctive feature: describe a change on its own terms — not a port / catch-up / comparison, never “X is too heavy” / “so you don’t need X”. Prior-art acknowledgment goes in roxygen @details (citing the method authors, not just a package); contributor credit goes in NEWS.md, by name, in prose. Justify a design/dependency choice by our own constraints (dependency-light, installable in webR for in-browser teaching) — never a judgment of another package’s weight or quality. Candid competitive/dependency analysis lives in pkgs/_roadmaps/datarium_feature_roadmap.md, not public git history.

Build & development commands

devtools::document()            # R/*.R roxygen -> man/*.Rd + NAMESPACE (run after any doc edit)
devtools::load_all()            # load datasets + docs for interactive checking
devtools::check()               # full R CMD check (what the R-CMD-check Action runs)
usethis::use_data(<name>)       # write data/<name>.rda from an in-memory frame (NEW datasets only)
rmarkdown::render("README.Rmd") # regenerate README.md after editing the topic list

Inspect one dataset: Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all(); data(anxiety); str(anxiety)'. No test suite; devtools::check() / the R-CMD-check Action is the gate. Don’t run document() with a roxygen version other than the pinned RoxygenNote in DESCRIPTION — it rewrites every .Rd.

Git & PR conventions

  • Everything lands through a PR off main; branch before the first commit. Stage only the specific changed files (git add the exact R/*.R / data/*.rda / NEWS.md / man/*.Rd), never git add -A. A local CLAUDE.md / .claude/ must never enter a commit. Fixes #N auto-closes; Refs #N links only.
  • Do NOT add “Co-Authored-By” / “Generated with…” / any AI-agent trailer to commits or PR/MR text. No emojis in commit/PR text — reads as authored solely by the maintainer.
  • External / community PRs — review first, then decide WITH the author. Never bulk-close. Read the diff; a close must cite a specific, verified reason. Credit contributors concretely (name + PR) in NEWS.

Package-specific

Overview. 21 curated teaching data frames spanning categorical data, regression, means comparison, the ANOVA family (independent / repeated / mixed), ANCOVA, proportions, and time series. No functions; NAMESPACE is an empty roxygen stub; base-R Depends only.

Architecture — each dataset is a synced triple: - data/<name>.rda — the lazy-loaded (LazyData: true) data frame (the taught bytes; see non-regression). - R/<name>.R — a roxygen-only doc stub ending in NULL (@name / @docType data / @usage data("<name>") / @format / @examples). - man/<name>.Rd — generated from the .R by roxygen; never hand-edit.

Provenance / generation (not shipped to CRAN builds where noted): - data-raw/<name>.R + source CSV — per-dataset reproducible build script (.Rbuildignored). - inst/data.R — authoring script for the contingency-derived sets (antismoking, taskachievment, renalstone), written with tidyverse + the counts_to_cases() helper at authoring time only (not a runtime dependency; simulated sets use set.seed()). - counts_to_cases() (documented in README.Rmd) expands a frequency/contingency table to case-level rows — the recovery pattern behind titanic.raw and housetasks.raw.

Conventions. - Datasets are a mix of base data.frame and tibble (as_tibble()); factors carry explicit levels (some ordered). Examples that must show base printing use head(as.data.frame(x)) (cf. anxiety) — preserve that. - Dotted names mark case-level recoveries (housetasks.raw, titanic.raw); id columns are id / participant. - docs/ is the built pkgdown site; README.md is generated from README.Rmd (knit it — don’t edit directly). inst/WORDLIST feeds the spell check.

Datasets by topic (README grouping; renalstone, taskachievment are newer additions): categorical — housetasks.raw, titanic.raw, antismoking; regression — marketing; two means — mice, mice2, genderweight; independent ANOVA — heartattack, headache, performance, jobsatisfaction; repeated ANOVA — selfesteem, selfesteem2, weightloss, depression; mixed ANOVA — anxiety; ANCOVA — stress; proportions — properties; contingency — taskachievment, renalstone; time series — AirPassengersDf.

R gotchas that have caused real bugs here

  • Byte-freeze traps: any resave/recompress (resaveRdaFiles, --resave-data, re-running an old use_data) silently changes .rda bytes and breaks lesson freezes. Check git status under data/ after any build step.
  • Adding a dataset needs the R/<name>.R stub too — otherwise R CMD check NOTEs “undocumented data” and the pkgdown reference is missing.
  • Tibble vs data.frame printing: several datasets are tibbles; an example expecting base-R print output must wrap with as.data.frame().
